newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's rates Matsuzakaya bonds Ba3.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Matsuzakaya bonds Ba3.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday that it had assigned a Ba3 rating to retailer Matsuzakaya Co Ltd's unsecured long-term bond issues.

Moody's gave the rating to Matsuzakaya's five billion yen 2.15 percent unsecured domestic bond due November 1999, its six billion yen 2.55 percent unsecured domestic bond due December 2000, and its 10 billion yen 0.65 percent unsecured domestic convertible bond due August 2003.

Moody's said the rating reflected Matsuzakaya's thin debt protection, anticipation of heightened competition in its main market, the likelihood Matsuzakaya would require a higher level of capital spending relative to cash flow to expand its store in Ueno, Tokyo, and Japan's weak retail environment.
Moody's said the rating also recognised Matsuzakaya's dominant position in its main market, and the company's close ties with its main bank, Tokai Bank Ltd, which was rated as A2 by Moody's.
This was the first time Moody's had rated Matsuzakaya's debt.
